ov: The one-humped camel, and the tallest of the three camel species. First domesticated in the Arabian Peninsula about 4,000 years ago, it has not lived wild for nearly 2,000 years, apart from a feral population in Australia.

why.dg: Generally non-aggressive, except for males in the rut.
why.et: Its meat and milk support several North African peoples.

rg: Dry regions of Africa, the Arabian Peninsula and the Thar Desert of India and Pakistan, plus a feral population in Australia.
df: Desert plants. It can lose more than 30% of its body water and survive.

cf.tip: The dromedary has one hump. The Bactrian camel has two and is up to a foot taller.

fx: Its hump is made of fat bound together by fibrous tissue, and stands 20 cm or more tall.
